meta_description: Build the circle of the 12 notes, one half step at a time, and find which different names sound the same.
title: Chromatic wheel
subtitle: The 12 notes, half step by half step, in one turn. Build the order note by note and find which different names sound the same — C♯ and D♭, E♯ and F.

wheel.half_title: Natural half step: there is no note between them

center.exp_sub: tap a slot or a name

ordem.title: Build the turn, one half step at a time
ordem.text_up: Pick the next note going up from the bank. Any name that sounds right counts — C♯ or D♭. When a sound enters the wheel, all of its names dim in the bank.
ordem.text_down: Pick the next note going down from the bank. Any name that sounds right counts — D♭ or C♯. When a sound enters the wheel, all of its names dim in the bank.

eq.title: What is the other name?
eq.text: The wheel is set with one name in each slot. For the marked slot, find in the bank the other way to write the same sound — or say there is none with a single accidental.

explorar.title: Listen and compare, no score
explorar.text: Tap a slot on the wheel or a name in the bank: every name of the same sound lights up together. Switch direction to see the in-between notes with ♯ or with ♭.

ladder.title: The ladder, from C to C
ladder.subtitle: the same wheel, opened into a line — notes appear as you get them right
ladder.aria: Ladder of the 12 notes, from C to C
ladder.half_title: half step: there is no note between them

cards.title: C D E F G A B
cards.text: Seven letters that repeat. Between almost every pair there is a whole step — and room for a note in between. Only E–F and B–C sit side by side: a half step.

cards.title: C♯ = D♭
cards.text: ♯ raises a half step, ♭ lowers a half step. The in-between note can be named from the neighbour below (rising, ♯) or from the one above (falling, ♭). On the violin: a half step is fingers touching.

cards.title: E♯ = F · B♯ = C
cards.text: And also F♭ = E and C♭ = B, because there is no note between them. D, G and A only get another name with a double accidental (𝄪 or 𝄫) — for later.

msg.ordem_start: Tap {start} in the bank. Then, at each step, the note a half step away.
msg.eq_tip: Think of the neighbouring note: the same sound can be “the one below + ♯” or “the one above + ♭”.
msg.explore_idle: Start with E or B: see that they also have a second name.
msg.explore_one: {a} is a whole step from each natural neighbour, so it has only one simple name.
msg.explore_black: {a} and {b} are the same sound: the note between {lo} and {hi}.
msg.explore_special: {a} and {b} are the same sound, because there is no note between E–F and B–C.
msg.ordem_done_up: Full turn! All 12 notes, rising from {start}. The next would be {start} again, an octave higher.
msg.ordem_done_down: Full turn! All 12 notes, falling from {start}. The next would be {start} again, an octave lower.
msg.ordem_special: Good! {label} sounds the same as {base} — between E and F (and between B and C) there is only a half step.
msg.ordem_alias_up: Good! {label} is the same sound as {other}. Rising, the custom is to write {pref}.
msg.ordem_alias_down: Good! {label} is the same sound as {other}. Falling, the custom is to write {pref}.
msg.ordem_black: Yes — {label}. The other name for this sound is {other}: notice it dimmed in the bank too.
msg.ordem_bad_same: {label} is the same note as {prev} — one sound with another name. Move up a half step.
msg.ordem_bad_up: {label} is {d} above {prev}. Look for the note just a half step away.
msg.ordem_bad_down: {label} is {d} below {prev}. Look for the note just a half step away.
msg.eq_ok_black: {shown} = {label}. It is the note between {lo} and {hi}: seen from below it is ♯, seen from above it is ♭.
msg.eq_ok_natural: {shown} = {label}. Between E–F and B–C there is only a half step, so ♯ or ♭ lands right on the neighbour.
msg.eq_ok_none: {shown} sits between two notes a whole step away, so there is no neighbouring letter a half step off. Another name only with a double accidental (𝄪/𝄫).
msg.eq_bad_self: That is the name already shown. Look for the other way to write the same sound.
msg.eq_bad_up: {label} sounds {d} above {shown}. The sound has to be the same.
msg.eq_bad_down: {label} sounds {d} below {shown}. The sound has to be the same.
msg.eq_none_black: Every in-between note has two names: one with ♯ and one with ♭.
msg.eq_none_natural: Remember E–F and B–C: only a half step between them.
